messages:
acme_infra: Hey team — since this morning (~09:12 UTC) we're seeing a batch of calls from our service routed to EU which adds ~200ms latency and some intermittent 401s. Sample request id: req_0a1b2c3. Our app uses the SDK and we set ?region=us-east-1 but a sidecar proxy injects X-Client-Region: eu. Can you confirm which wins in routing and whether this could cause auth failures?

maria_support: Thanks — can you paste a raw request example and the SDK version? Any failing request IDs helps.

acme_infra: Here's a minimal repro (we scrubbed tokens):

curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?region=us-east-1" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_REDACTED" \n  -H "X-Client-Region: eu" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"hello"}'

SDK version: 1.4.2
Sample req IDs: req_0a1b2c3, req_0d4e5f6

kevin_sdk: cc @maria_support @daniel_sre — this matches a bug we shipped in SDK v1.4.2. When the SDK sees both a config-level region and a request-level region/query-param, we reversed precedence in one code path and end up writing X-Client-Region from the last-set config. If a proxy also injects a conflicting header, the header ends up winning.

Repro (JS):

const client = new Redwood({ region: 'us-east-1' });
// proxy adds header X-Client-Region: eu
await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi', region: 'us-east-1' });

Workarounds: upgrade to 1.4.3 (patch ready) or remove the injected header at the proxy. Also setting env REDWOOD_REGION explicitly to the intended region mitigates.

daniel_sre: I pulled the routing logs for req_0a1b2c3 — trace shows: routed -> eu-prod-2 because X-Client-Region=eu was present. Our routing order today is: header > query param > IP geo. That explains the extra hop and the occasional 401 (token bound to us region). Trace link (internal): https://internal.redwood/traces/req_0a1b2c3

archana_ops: Temporary mitigation for customers: ensure the proxy does not set X-Client-Region, or align it with the query param. If you can't change the proxy quickly, remove the per-request header in the SDK by setting client-level config and upgrading.

maria_support: I'm documenting this for the support ticket: "If both a region header and a region param are present, the header currently takes precedence. Ensure both match or remove the header." Escalating to eng to add a diagnostic warning.

jenna_product: Suggestion: add a soft diagnostic header in responses when header/param disagree (e.g., X-Region-Conflict: 1) and emit a metric so we can catch customers hitting this. Full 4xx change would be breaking; soft signal first. @kevin_sdk please estimate.

kevin_sdk: I have a patch for SDK behavior (1.4.3) that fixes precedence and will add a deprecation/diagnostic header in the server. Estimate: 1 day to push the SDK patch and 2 days for server-side soft-signal rollout. PR: #2345 (cutting release now).

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: sdk/1.4.3 published at 1824501250 — npm/pypi rollout started :rocket:

acme_infra: Thanks, we'll remove the proxy header and test with 1.4.3. Appreciate the quick turnaround :heart:

maria_support: Please re-open if you still see misrouting after upgrade and header removal. I'll close the support ticket after your confirmation.
